name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=battle, descriptor=set_battle_anim_phase_to_1. The trailing '1' is the literal value written to data_fd2_battle_anim_phase (a semantic constant), NOT a Ghidra address residue -- 1 is not a hex address and matches the body MOV [0x51A83],1. Name accurately reflects the sole action (set the battle animation phase flag to 1).
purpose: Shared tail stub that sets the global battle animation-phase flag (data_fd2_battle_anim_phase) to 1.
logic_summary: Three-instruction tail: ADD ESP,0xC (drops the 3 dword args the caller pushed for the preceding 3-arg warp helper), MOV dword [0x51A83],1 (battle_anim_phase=1), RET. In the original binary it is a JMP/CALL target shared by multiple chapter cinematic handlers; the emitted C is a plain void setter performing just the flag write (data_fd2_battle_anim_phase = 1), with the arg cleanup subsumed by the C calling convention. Functionally equivalent.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect: data_fd2_battle_anim_phase := 1.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct and concise but minimal -- it did not state the 3-arg (ADD ESP,0xC) cleanup origin nor name the emitted consumer, so the rationale for emitting a standalone setter (vs. inlining) was implicit.
notes: Sole emitted CALL caller: fd2_chapter_event_handler_52__ch30_major_cinematic (@0x35F92), calls it on both return branches (xrefs @0x36073, @0x36083). Verified the plate's previously-unverified Class-3 alt-entry claims via xrefs: alt_3 @0x35C18 reached by UNCONDITIONAL_JUMP from fd2_chapter_event_handler_17 (@0x348F7) and fd2_chapter_event_handler_25 (@0x34D63); alt_D @0x35C22 reached by CONDITIONAL_JUMP from fd2_chapter_event_handler_17 (@0x3488A). Updated the Ghidra plate to record these as verified and drop the stale 'verify if needed' caveat. data_fd2_battle_anim_phase @0x51A83 is a shared uint32 game-state flag (globals.h), written/read by many functions (dialog.c, main.c, spelleff.c, input.c, cursor.c) -- not unique to this stub; no rename concern for the global. This function is also catalogued in open_issues.md as a benign SHARED EPILOGUE STUB; emit pipeline impact on the binary is zero.
